key_insight: A geometry-conditioned surrogate can learn spray breakup by using AMR refinement structure as a compact proxy for interface dynamics in transient two-phase flow.
engineering_relevance: This enables much faster nozzle design exploration by approximating expensive VOF-VOF/AMR CFD simulations while retaining key breakup behavior.
method: Train on 797 nozzle simulations with geometry-conditioned latent encoding.
Use AMR cell-density field as the main learned representation of where the solver refines the flow.
Reconstruct transient density/interface evolution first, then recover remaining flow variables with a lightweight second stage.
evidence_signal: On held-out simulations, the model captures key interface dynamics and predicts each trajectory in 0.045 seconds, over 6×10^4 faster than Basilisk CFD.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well AMR refinement patterns generalize to new nozzle geometries and breakup regimes not seen in training.
paper_title: Learning Interface Breakup: A Geometry-Conditioned Latent Surrogate for Spray Formation
